Keywords: ga4 event tracking custom events gtag measurement protocol user actions
Description: GA4 is event-based (unlike UA sessions). Every user action should be tracked as an event with parameters. GA4 auto-collects basic events; you must manually add custom events for business-critical actions.
Implementation: Auto events: page_view, first_visit, session_start. Enhanced measurement: scroll, outbound click, file download, video. Custom: use gtag('event', 'event_name', {param: value}) or push via GTM.
Report Path: Admin → Data Streams → Enhanced Measurement / DebugView for testing
Do: Tag all business-critical actions (purchase, lead, signup, form submit). Use GTM for custom events to avoid dev dependency. Test in DebugView before publishing.
Dont: Don't rely on auto-events alone for conversions. Don't create duplicate events with different names. Don't use spaces in event names (use underscores).

Keywords: ga4 conversions key events goals purchase lead form submit sign up
Description: GA4 calls conversions 'Key Events'. You mark any event as a Key Event and it appears in Conversions reports. Critical for optimization and Google Ads integration.
Implementation: In GA4: Admin → Events → Mark as Key Event. Recommended key events: purchase, generate_lead, sign_up, begin_checkout, add_to_cart.
Do: Mark only meaningful business actions as Key Events (not every page view). For e-commerce, use the standard purchase event with value parameter. Link to Google Ads for conversion import.
Dont: Don't mark too many events as Key Events (makes reports cluttered). Don't forget to set currency in data stream settings. Don't omit value parameter on revenue events.

Keywords: user acquisition source medium campaign traffic channel first visit new users
Description: Shows how new users discovered your site — which channel, source, and campaign brought them for the first time. Uses first-touch attribution.
Implementation: No setup needed. Just segment by First user source/medium/campaign. Filter: New Users only.
Do: Compare channel performance for new user volume. Export to Looker Studio for client reporting. Look for trends by cohort (weekly).
Dont: Don't confuse 'User Acquisition' (first touch) with 'Traffic Acquisition' (session-level). Don't exclude branded search — it shows brand health.

Keywords: traffic acquisition session source medium channel traffic returning users all sessions
Description: Session-level attribution — which channels brought traffic in each session (not just first visit). Best for day-to-day traffic analysis.
Implementation: No setup needed. Primary dimensions: Session source/medium, Session default channel grouping.
Do: Use default channel groupings for high-level view. Drill into source/medium for detail. Compare periods to spot trends. Look for drops in key channels.
Dont: Don't use this as your only attribution view — it's last-touch by default. Don't ignore direct traffic (often includes UTM errors or dark social).

Keywords: funnel analysis conversion funnel exploration steps drop off completion rate
Description: Visualize how users progress through a multi-step process (signup, checkout, onboarding). Shows drop-off at each step and where to optimize.
Implementation: Explore → Funnel Exploration. Define steps using events. Choose open (any path between steps) or closed (must follow exact sequence). Set step conditions.
Do: Test different funnel configurations (strict vs open). Use segments to compare device types or traffic sources. Look for large drop-offs — these are your optimization priorities.
Dont: Don't use page views as funnel steps if you have event data (events are more reliable). Don't set up too many steps (5-7 is manageable).

Keywords: ga4 audience segment remarketing google ads users behavior condition
Description: Create segments of users based on behavior, events, or attributes. Use for retargeting in Google Ads, personalization, or reporting analysis.
Implementation: Admin → Audiences → New Audience. Use pre-built templates or build custom. Common audiences: All Users, Purchasers, High-Intent Visitors (viewed pricing + didn't convert), Cart Abandoners.
Do: Link GA4 to Google Ads to use audiences for ad targeting. Create high-intent audiences (pricing page + no purchase). Build lookalike audiences in Google Ads from your purchaser segment.
Dont: Don't create audiences without enabling GA4 ↔ Google Ads link. Don't create too many audiences (GA4 limit: 100 per property). Don't use broad audiences for high-value retargeting.

Keywords: path exploration user journey sequence what page next behavior discovery
Description: See what pages or events users visit before and after any specific point. Discovery tool for understanding user behavior flows.
Implementation: Explore → Path Exploration. Set starting point (event or page) or ending point. Drill down into specific branches.
Do: Use to find: what pages users visit before converting, what they do after landing from a specific campaign, where users go after exiting a key page.
Dont: Don't use path as your primary analysis tool (it's exploratory, not precise). Don't forget to filter by segment to see different user types.

Keywords: utm parameters campaign tracking source medium campaign term content attribution url builder
Description: UTM parameters tag your traffic sources so GA4 can correctly attribute sessions. Without them, email, social, and referral traffic often misattributes to 'direct'.
Implementation: Add UTM tags to all non-organic links: ?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=paid_social&utm_campaign=spring_sale. Use Google's Campaign URL Builder. Create naming conventions and enforce them.
Report Path: Reports → Traffic Acquisition → Session source/medium (filtered to your UTM names)
Do: Create a UTM naming convention document. Tag ALL external links (email, social, ads, partnerships). Use lowercase only (case-sensitive in GA4). Store all UTMs in a tracking spreadsheet.
Dont: Don't use spaces in UTM values (use hyphens or underscores). Don't forget UTMs on email campaigns (email traffic shows as direct without them). Don't vary capitalization (facebook ≠ Facebook).

Keywords: ecommerce tracking purchase revenue transaction product item ga4
Description: Track purchase events with product-level detail: item names, IDs, prices, quantities, categories. Required for revenue reporting and ROAS calculations.
Implementation: Implement purchase event with items array: gtag('event', 'purchase', {transaction_id, value, currency, items: [{item_id, item_name, price, quantity}]}). Best done via GTM + dataLayer.
Do: Always include item-level data (not just total value). Include transaction_id to prevent duplicate counting. Test in DebugView → Monetization. Use Shopify/WooCommerce GA4 plugins for CMS sites.
Dont: Don't omit currency parameter (GA4 defaults to USD otherwise). Don't double-fire purchase events (can inflate revenue). Don't ignore refund events for accurate revenue reporting.

Keywords: looker studio data studio dashboard report visualization ga4 client report
Description: Connect GA4 data to Looker Studio (formerly Data Studio) for custom dashboards, client reporting, and multi-source data blending.
Implementation: In Looker Studio: Create new report → Add data → Google Analytics 4. Select property and date range. Use GA4 dimensions and metrics as fields. Blend with Google Ads, Search Console, and Sheets data.
Do: Build reusable templates (duplicate for new clients). Use comparison date ranges for easy YoY/MoM views. Blend GA4 with Google Ads for full funnel cost-to-conversion view.
Dont: Don't build one-off reports without templates. Don't use default GA4 reports for client delivery — Looker Studio is much better. Don't forget to set data refresh schedule.
